newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mandela says party will name successor.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela says party will name successor.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela has told members of his African National Congress they will decide who succeeds him as party leader, state radio said.

The South African Broadcasting Corporation quoted sources at a weekend meeting of the ANC's national executive committee as saying Mandela told delegates he had not endorsed Deputy President Thabo Mbeki to be the next party leader.
Mandela, 78, has previously described Mbeki as the kind of person who could step into his shoes. Mandela plans to resign when general elections are held in 1999.
"Mandela says democratic procedures will be followed in the election of both the ANC leader and president of the country when he steps down," the SABC said.
"He says he will leave the issue of his successor as party leader to the ANC congress, which is to be held next year."
Many political and economic commentators had in recent months taken it as read that Mbeki would succeed Mandela.
The ANC could not immediately be reached for comment on the radio report. An official party statement on the NEC meeting made no mention of the succession.
